sources.entry: playwright-python - Python version of the Playwright testing and automation library.

summary.one_liner: Python library for automating Chromium, Firefox and WebKit browsers through a single API, with both sync and async interfaces.
summary.what_it_does: Provides the Python binding for Playwright, a browser automation library that drives Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. The README shows how to launch each browser type, open a page, navigate to a URL, and take a screenshot. It offers a synchronous API (playwright.sync_api) and an asynchronous API (playwright.async_api) built on asyncio. The README's support table lists Chromium, WebKit and Firefox as working on Linux, macOS and Windows. The README also points to Node.js, .NET and Java versions of Playwright for users who prefer those languages. Detailed docs and the API reference are linked from the README but not included in it.
use_cases: automate browser actions in Python scripts
take screenshots of web pages in multiple browsers
cross-browser testing across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
scrape or interact with JavaScript-heavy websites
how_to_run: Run the sync example: from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, then use sync_playwright() as p and p.chromium.launch()
Run the async example: from playwright.async_api import async_playwright and await browser_type.launch() inside asyncio.run(main())
notable: Single API controls Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
Both synchronous and asynchronous Python APIs
Supports Linux, macOS and Windows per the README support table
Same library family is available for Node.js, .NET and Java
caveats: The README does not include the full documentation or API reference inline; it links out to them
Browser binaries must be installed separately before use, based on the example flow
